solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Air also moves in commotion

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
also means and, in addition
dance moves, or simply to move rhythmically, is to dance

explanation.surface: A breeze stirs things up amid some general uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' and 'moves' read as wind blowing; they are a tune and dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: making a big fuss or palaver over something is making a song and dance of it.

clue.text: Very minor railway is sinking

parts.note: sub- means below or under, lesser in rank
a siding is a minor railway track off the main line

explanation.surface: A tiny branch line is subsiding into the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling downward or sinking is subsiding, as ground does.

clue.text: Significant agreement about terms of Government scheme

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the agreement goes round the other letters

parts.note: a nod shows agreement

indicators.note: terms are ends, here the last letters of the two words

explanation.surface: An important deal concerning the conditions of a state plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Something notable, famous or significant is noted.

clue.text: Joint in which anger's not right

indicators.note: not right means the letter for right is removed

parts.note: to rankle is to cause anger

explanation.surface: A sore joint where bad temper is out of place.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint between foot and leg.

clue.text: Pessimist is more so, with day going wrong

indicators.note: going wrong suggests disorder, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A gloomy person is even more so on a bad day.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet of doom always predicting disaster is a pessimist.

clue.text: Medicinal fluid: sick man rues swallowing it up

indicators.note: swallowing means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other
sick suggests being unwell or disordered, so the letters are jumbled
in a down clue, up means the word is written upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: An ill man regrets having to gulp his medicine down.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads upwards; 'swallowing' puts that piece in the middle of the shuffled 'man rues' letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood serum containing antibodies, used as a medical treatment.

clue.text: That man in church, getting Rector's encouragement

indicators.note: the man is placed inside the church

parts.note: CE, Church of England
he is that man

explanation.surface: A man at church receives the vicar's supportive words.
explanation.definitionFit: A shout of support or comfort is a cheer.

clue.text: Jocularity's hard after disappointment getting split contract

indicators.note: after means the jocularity comes after the disappointment in the answer

parts.note: a comedown is a letdown or disappointment
wit is humour or jocularity
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Humour gets tough after a letdown over a disputed deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting split' tells you the comedown is divided into two words; 'contract' is the verb, as in catching an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract an illness is to catch it or fall ill with it.

clue.text: Soldiers had an effect in area of influence

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for ordinary soldiers
something that bit took hold or had an effect

explanation.surface: Troops made an impact within a zone they controlled.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a sphere of power or control is someone's orbit.

clue.text: Most complicated speed restrictions will take a little time

parts.note: a knot is a unit of speed at sea
ties are bonds or restrictions
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Elaborate speed limits will cause a short delay.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of knotty, meaning tangled or intricate, so hardest to unravel.

clue.text: Organised fighting to follow with others left in ring, ultimately

parts.note: to tag along is to follow
the rest are the others

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of ring

explanation.surface: Arranged bouts with others still in the ring at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A staged team wrestling format where partners take turns in the ring.

clue.text: Who could be so reviled?

indicators.note: what the letters could be once rearranged; the clue invites a reshuffle of the letters of so reviled

explanation.surface: A question asking which people might attract such scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: wrongdoers are those who get reviled.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked wrongdoers are exactly the sort of people likely to be reviled.

clue.text: Trimmed bush beside front of garden gets indifferent response

indicators.note: a trimmed word has had its end clipped off, as a hedge is cut back

parts.note: a shrub is a bush

indicators.note: the front of garden is its first letter

explanation.surface: A clipped hedge by the garden entrance gets a so-what reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: A gesture of the shoulders signalling not caring is an indifferent reply.

clue.text: Republicans brought in mixed offering, having gutted largely controlled market

indicators.note: the Republicans are brought into the medley, placed inside it

parts.note: an olio is a hotchpotch or mixed dish
GOP, the Grand Old Party, is the US Republican Party

indicators.note: gutting a word removes its insides, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Politicians handed over a jumbled deal after stripping a mostly regulated market.
explanation.definitionFit: Economics term: a market dominated by a few suppliers who control it.

clue.text: Live in a difficult situation?

definitions.meaning: as broadcast live, happening there and then at the scene
put under pressure or in a tight corner

explanation.surface: A query about being in a broadcast or in a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both at the scene immediately and put in an awkward position.

clue.text: Not emotionally involved in the end

definitions.meaning: an aim or goal is an end

explanation.surface: Detached until the final moment.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means impartial; as a noun, a goal or target.

clue.text: More mature Government will avoid complaint, right?

indicators.note: avoiding the Government means the word complaint is written without its letter for it

parts.note: a gripe is a complaint

explanation.surface: A wiser administration will steer clear of grumbling, won't it?
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of ripe, meaning fully developed or mature.

clue.text: Input into machine issuing notes?

parts.note: the machine sounds like a cash dispenser handing out banknotes, but the notes are musical ones from a pianola

explanation.surface: Feeding something into a cash machine that dispenses banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: A perforated paper roll fed into a player piano produces the music played.

clue.text: Opposite pole to vision? Darkness

indicators.note: south swapped for the other pole, north, so one compass letter replaces its opposite

parts.note: sight is vision

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what is the reverse of seeing: darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: Night-time is the dark part of the day.

clue.text: Heartless judge misread terrible tales of woe

indicators.note: a heartless word has lost its middle, leaving just its outer letters
terrible signals the letters of misread are badly mangled

explanation.surface: An unfeeling judge misinterpreted some sad stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misread' looks like the surface verb but is the fodder; 'terrible' is what shuffles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeremiad, after the prophet Jeremiah's Lamentations, is a long mournful complaint.

clue.text: No major show will fail to feature a lion, say

indicators.note: failing to feature the animal means its letters are left out of the word for show

parts.note: to indicate is to show
a lion is an example of a big cat

explanation.surface: A minor production won't manage to include a lion in its cast.
explanation.definitionFit: An independent record label or film company is one that is not one of the majors.

clue.text: Coastal feature, obstruction mostly limiting entrance to tide

indicators.note: limiting means enclosing, so the shortened word surrounds the letter
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: a delay is a hold-up or obstruction

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A shoreline landform mostly blocks the tide from coming in.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan of river sediment at a river's mouth, shaped like the Greek letter.

clue.text: Medicinal stuff: a supply, running short, is lashed by wind

indicators.note: lashed by the winding rope, so the supply is bound inside the coil

parts.note: to wind is to coil

indicators.note: running short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a store is a supply

explanation.surface: A medicine stock, dwindling, gets battered by a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' looks like a gale but rhymes with 'kind' here: the verb to coil, whose letters wrap round the shortened supply.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil from the castor bean, long used as a laxative remedy.

clue.text: Pole incorporating point?

indicators.note: incorporating means taking in, so the pole holds the point

parts.note: a spar is a pole
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A query whether a staff has a sharp tip built in.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a weapon that is a shaft with a sharp tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A throwing weapon is a long shaft with a sharpened head.

clue.text: Pious but not good, imprisoning daughter in a strange way

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding inside, so the shortened word encloses the letter
but not good means removing the letter for good

parts.note: godly means pious

explanation.surface: A devout but wicked person locks up their child, which is weird.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverb meaning peculiarly or strangely.

clue.text: There'll be a reduction in the damage at this rate

definitions.text: There'll be a reduction in the damage at this rate

parts.words: There'll be a reduction in the damage at this rate
parts.note: the damage is slang for what something costs, so a cut in it is a discount on the cost

explanation.surface: A grim forecast of harm lessening at the present pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damage' reads as harm; in British slang 'what's the damage?' asks the price.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling at fifty percent off the usual cost is a sale reduction.

clue.text: Landlubber's ending in drink — and may do this

definitions.text: Landlubber's ending in drink — and may do this

indicators.note: the final letter sits inside the word for drink

parts.note: to down a drink is to swallow it

indicators.note: a word's ending is its last letter

explanation.surface: A non-sailor who ends up in the sea might well perish there.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Landlubber's means 'is': the landlubber's last letter is put in DOWN, and the whole clue describes his likely fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot swim, ending up in the water, may die by suffocation in it.

clue.text: Fierce fights lost with betrayal, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so these letters end up jumbled

explanation.surface: Bitter conflicts were lost through treachery, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-for-all brawl or bitter contest is a battle royal; plural for fights.
